chunks.text: When you arrive at the hospital, the first thing you need to do is check in at the reception desk.
The receptionist will ask for your basic information.
The receptionist may ask, what is your full name?
What is your date of birth?
What is the reason for your visit?
You can say, my name is Emily Johnson.
I have a fever and a bad cough.
After checking in, you may be asked to wait in the waiting room until a doctor is ready to see you.
When you see the doctor, you need to explain how you feel.
The doctor may ask, what's wrong?
Are you allergic to any medicine?
You can say, I have a stomach ache and nausea.
I feel very weak and tired.
I have had a headache for two days.
Yes, I have a fever of 39 degrees Celsius.
No, I am not allergic to any medicine.
Sore throat, pain in your throat.
Runny nose when your nose is dripping.
Dizziness, feeling like you will fall.
The doctor will ask more questions and give you advice.
The doctor may say, let me check your temperature.
I will take your blood pressure.
You need to drink more water and rest.
I will prescribe some medicine for you.
You can ask, is my condition serious?
What should I do to feel better?
If the doctor gives you a prescription, you need to go to the pharmacy to get your medicine.
The doctor or nurse may say, take this medicine three times a day.
You need antibiotics for five days.
You can buy this at the pharmacy.
You can ask, how often should I take this?
Do I need to take this with food?
Where can I find the pharmacy?
Can I take this if I am pregnant?
If you have a medical emergency, you need to ask for help quickly.
If you call an ambulance, you can say, I need an ambulance.
In the emergency room, you can say, I have chest pain.
When your treatment is finished, you may need instructions for recovery.
The doctor may say, you need to rest for a few days.
Come back for a checkup next week.
Avoid junk food and drink more water.
You can ask, when can I go back to work?
Can I get a medical report for work?
The person who helps the doctor.
A sick person in the hospital.
The person at the front desk.
X -ray room for checking broken bones.
Intensive care unit for serious patients.
Now you know how to speak English at the hospital.
One, stay calm in medical situations.
Two, learn common symptoms and medical words.
Always ask questions if you don't understand.
I hope this episode helps you feel more confident if you ever need to visit a hospital in an English -speaking country.
